reqs.text: For the classroom, if you can spare them.
Ferry folk always need something. Today it's this.
Turnip ate the last batch. Please don't ask how.

mail.title: You're invited: Lantern Night
mail.text:
Lantern Night is on summer 14, down at the ferry after sunset. Bring a wish. Fen says bring two in case the first one sinks.

Odile

mail.title: Tomorrow is my birthday
mail.text:
It's my birthday tomorrow. Don't make a fuss.

Unless the fuss involves honey, or a Hearth Tonic, in which case fuss away.

Mara

mail.title: You're invited: Flower Dance
mail.text:
The Flower Dance is on spring 14, from dusk in the village square. Wear something nice. The cat is also invited, though historically it has not danced.

Odile

mail.title: Tomorrow is my birthday
mail.text:
MY BIRTHDAY IS TOMORROW!!!

I like jam. And starfruit. And honey. Just so you know. No reason.

Pip

mail.title: You're invited: Star Feast
mail.text:
The Star Feast is on winter 14, in the square. Everyone brings a gift for the secret swap. You'll find out whose name you drew when you arrive.

Odile

mail.title: Tomorrow is my birthday
mail.text:
Tomorrow is my birthday. I'm told teachers shouldn't have a favourite flower, but mine is the moonpetal.

Odile

mail.title: You're invited: Harvest Fair
mail.text:
The Harvest Fair judging is on autumn 14. Enter your finest thing: a crop, a fish, a potion, anything. I am a judge this year, so I can't be seen to favour you. (Good luck.)

Odile

mail.title: Tomorrow is my birthday
mail.text:
It's my birthday tomorrow! The bees made me a cake. (They didn't.)

If you ever find a Starshard, I collect them.

Wren

mail.title: Tomorrow is my birthday
mail.text:
Birthday tomorrow. Stopped counting years ago.

If a moonfish swims your way, I wouldn't say no.

Fen

mail.title: You're invited: Lantern Night
mail.text:
Lantern Night is on summer 14, down at the ferry after sunset. Bring a wish. Fen says bring two in case the first one sinks.

Odile

mail.title: I drew you a cat
mail.text:
I drew you a picture of the cat. Also I found some seeds in Ma's flour bin. They're yours now. Don't tell Ma.

Pip

mail.title: A little warmth
mail.text:
You've done so much for me and Turnip. Bramble taught me one spell, the only one I ever learned: a little warmth for tired bones. I've written it out for you. I never could make it work myself.

Mara

mail.title: The Old Wood
mail.text:
Your aunt foraged in the Old Wood every morning. There's a gate on the west side of your garden, past the fence. Mushrooms in spring, berries in summer, all sorts.

Mind the brambles at the top. They only open for those the Wood knows.

Fen

mail.title: Your aunt's spellbook
mail.text:
To the new witch of Brambleroot,

Among your aunt's papers we found her spellbook, which by Guild law now passes to you. Most of its pages are blank. Spells are learned, not copied: your neighbours and the Wood will teach you the rest.

The first page holds Quicken. Mana returns each night while you sleep.

The Witches' Guild, Registry Office

y1s1.txt: Your lantern drifts downriver, glowing gold. Tonight every growing crop in your garden will grow an extra day.

y1s2.txt: Your Bellmelon takes second place, just behind Wren's honey cake. 700 coins.

y1s3.txt: Wren opens your Bellmelon. They beam and tuck it away carefully. Then Pip slides a parcel across the table: a Starshard and 200 coins, wrapped in a page of an old almanac.

y2s0.txt: Odile counts the steps under her breath, then forgets to, and dances better for it. Afterwards, Pip crowns you with daisies and tells you it is very important to keep it on. Odile lent you a weather almanac. You'll see tomorrow's weather when you go to bed.

y2s1.txt: Your lantern catches on a reed, and when you go to free it you find a purse someone lost years ago: 800 coins.
